note: Built from union contracts, city/county records, recruiting material and news, cross-checked against a union member's statewide survey (Oct. 2026). 'Reported' means a credible claim without a public document yet.

departments.name: Kissimmee Fire Department
departments.detail: First Central Florida department on 24/72. The city launched its new D-shift on April 25, 2026 after hiring 49 firefighters, paid for with a fire assessment fee.

departments.name: Pasco County Fire Rescue
departments.detail: Launched its D-shift (24 on / 72 off) in January 2026.

departments.name: Gainesville Fire Rescue
departments.detail: Moved from three platoons to four (24/72) on Aug. 19, 2024, per the department's 2024 annual report. The later IAFF contract kept the schedule.

departments.name: Levy County Fire Rescue
departments.detail: Commissioners approved 24/72 in September 2025, and the Department of Public Safety completed the switch for fire and EMS crews in September 2026. The county's own webpage still says 24/48 and hasn't been updated.

departments.name: Lake County Fire Rescue (EMS only)
departments.detail: Paramedics and EMTs moved to 24/72 in August 2025. Firefighters are not yet included (see In talks).

departments.name: Marion County Fire Rescue
departments.detail: Contract approved June 2, 2026 commits the county to 24/72 by October 2029, hiring nearly 250 people for a D-shift. Current job postings say crews work 24/48 until the transition.

departments.name: Ocala Fire Rescue
departments.detail: City contract with IAFF Local 2135, approved Aug. 18, 2026, commits to a 42-hour 24/72 schedule by Sept. 30, 2029. Until then crews stay on a half-Kelly Day schedule averaging about 52 hours a week.

departments.name: Polk County Fire Rescue
departments.detail: Firefighters' contract secures a D-shift (24/72, 42 hours) no later than Oct. 1, 2027, and the paramedics' union reached a matching tentative deal in October 2026. Both still need union ratification and a county commission vote.

departments.name: St. Johns County Fire Rescue
departments.detail: IAFF Local 3865 is pushing for 24/72 plus about 125 hires. Talks went to impasse in January 2026 and were still in the state impasse process as of May 2026.

departments.name: Lake County Fire Rescue (firefighters)
departments.detail: IAFF Local 3990 is working to move dual-certified firefighter/paramedics onto the same 24/72 schedule EMS staff already have.

departments.name: Orlando Fire Department
departments.detail: A 42-hour week was a key issue in 2025 bargaining (a fourth platoon would need about 135 more firefighters). The November 2025 contract kept a 48-hour week, so it remains a future goal.

departments.name: Boynton Beach Fire Rescue
departments.detail: City hiring material lists a 24/72 schedule averaging 2,190 hours a year. The commission approved the switch in 2022 and it took effect in 2023.

departments.name: Delray Beach Fire Rescue
departments.detail: Emergency Operations firefighters work a 42-hour week on 24 on / 72 off, starting Oct. 1, 2025, under the union contract.

departments.name: Palm Beach County Fire Rescue
departments.detail: The union contract moves 24-hour crews to 24/72 at 42 hours in January 2027 (the county can push this to April 2027). The county funded Phase 1 positions in FY2026, and the full change needs about 148 more positions.

departments.name: Greenacres Fire Rescue
departments.detail: Not a straight 24/72: it is adopting a four-platoon, 42-hour 'Spartan' schedule (24 on/96 off/24 on/48 off), set to begin Oct. 1, 2026. The start isn't confirmed yet.

departments.name: Jacksonville Fire and Rescue
departments.detail: The union is pushing for a 42-hour week, which it says would take a fourth shift of about 450 firefighters. The chief says no immediate change is planned; the current contract runs to 2027.

departments.name: Indian River County Fire Rescue
departments.detail: County leaders are discussing a 42-hour week, estimated at 68 more firefighters and about $11 million, phased in over a few years. No plan adopted yet.

departments.name: Tampa Fire Rescue
departments.detail: The 2025–2028 contract keeps a 48-hour week with Kelly Days but adds flex days in 2027 and 2028 explicitly as a step toward a reduced work week.

departments.name: Boca Raton Fire Rescue
departments.detail: Has worked 24 on / 72 off for decades, according to Palm Beach Gardens' fire chief in 2024 coverage of neighboring departments' schedules.

departments.name: North Collier Fire Rescue
departments.detail: 2025–2028 contract put the Rescue Division on 24/72 at ratification (Oct. 2025) and requires Operations to move to a four-platoon 24/72 no later than Oct. 1, 2026.

departments.name: Palm Beach Gardens Fire Rescue
departments.detail: The FY2026 budget added 23 firefighters for a four-shift 24/72 system, with crews moving to a 42-hour week in October 2026. The actual start date hasn't been confirmed.

departments.name: Deerfield Beach (new city fire department)
departments.detail: City voted in January 2026 to leave Broward Sheriff's Fire Rescue. Its new department is recruiting now, advertising 24/72 shifts, with operations expected around fall 2027.

departments.name: Highland Beach Fire Rescue
departments.detail: An October 2024 town commission packet states fire rescue personnel work 24-hour shifts followed by 72 hours off, with leave rules written for 42-hour shift employees.

departments.name: Tamarac Fire Rescue
departments.detail: The 2024–2027 contract keeps 24/48 but requires the city to meet the union by Oct. 25, 2026 to discuss moving to 24/72, including costs and staffing.

departments.name: Tavares Fire Department
departments.detail: Crews work 24/48 now. A proposed 24/72 schedule would start April 1, 2028, pending council funding approval, and an August 2026 contract set up a committee to study the 42-hour week.

departments.name: Miramar Fire Rescue
departments.detail: The city's 2026 firefighter recruiting (through its testing partner) advertises 'Now Offering 24/72 Schedule.' The city's own pages don't state the rotation.

departments.name: Titusville Fire Department
departments.detail: City Council approved the 2025–2028 IAFF Local 2445 contract on May 12, 2026; it includes a move to a 24/72 schedule starting in 2027. Exact start date not stated.

departments.name: Gilchrist County Fire Rescue
departments.detail: Hiring now, with a new 24/72 schedule set to begin Jan. 5, 2027, according to a regional union post. No county document confirming it has been found yet.

departments.name: St. Cloud Fire Rescue
departments.detail: City recruiting page says crews work 24/48 and that the City Council is reviewing funding strategies to support a move to 24/72.

departments.name: Coral Springs-Parkland Fire Department
departments.detail: A city command-level job description lists helping implement new staffing models and schedules, 'e.g., 24/72 or 42-hour work week.' No approved start date found.

departments.name: Ponce Inlet Fire Department
departments.detail: A July 2025 town budget workshop studied moving from 24/48 (about 56 hours) to a four-shift 42-hour model. Any change would need bargaining and funding.

departments.name: Seminole Tribe Fire Rescue
departments.detail: Reported by department members (on LinkedIn and by word of mouth) to have worked 24/72 for over 20 years. No public tribal document confirms it.

departments.name: Ocoee Fire Department
departments.detail: A union-compiled survey says Ocoee's FY2026 budget modeled 24/72 costs and estimated up to 21 more firefighters would be needed. The city's budget file couldn't be opened to confirm, and nothing has been approved.
